title: TRUNK-6842: Void encounter providers after the encounter void details are set
body:
Follow-up to #6710.

## Description of what I changed
In `EncounterServiceImpl.voidEncounter`, the encounter providers are now voided after the encounter's `voidedBy`, `dateVoided` and `voidReason` are set, instead of before.

When `voidEncounter` is called from within the API, for example by `transferEncounter`, AOP is bypassed and the encounter's `voidedBy`/`dateVoided` are still null when the old loop ran. The encounter providers were then voided with null void details. `VoidSaveHandler` later filled these in on save with a new timestamp, which can differ from the encounter's `dateVoided`. When they differ, the unvoid handler won't restore those encounter providers.

#6739 (2.9.x) and #6740 (master) already include this change.

https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/TRUNK-6842

title: maven(deps): bump org.owasp.encoder:encoder from 1.5.1 to 1.6.0
body:
Bumps [org.owasp.encoder:encoder](https://github.com/OWASP/owasp-java-encoder) from 1.5.1 to 1.6.0.
Release notes

Sourced from org.owasp.encoder:encoder's releases.

OWASP Java Encoder 1.6.0

OWASP Java Encoder 1.6.0 reduces unnecessary JavaScript letter escaping while retaining recognized HTML-token protection across trusted fragments. It resolves #243 through #247. This is a minor release because emitted bytes and streaming behavior change.

Changes and migration

  • forJavaScript and forJavaScriptBlock keep interior script-name letters readable. A final C, I, P, R, S, or T in either case still receives an escape. Punctuation and whitespace escapes remain.
  • http://google.com now produces http:\/\/google.com; script becomes scrip\x74; i remains \x69. The rule is conservative: cat becomes ca\x74.
  • HTML does not remove whitespace inside tag names. Escaping < in a complete value addresses the HTML tag delimiter concern, but a fragment may have its < supplied by trusted text. The terminal escape preserves that supported protection.
  • General/block EncodedWriter callers must flush before writing directly to the wrapped writer. Explicit flushes safely emit pending letters/surrogates and can add escapes while preserving the JavaScript UTF-16 value. Low-level callers must retain unread input after UNDERFLOW and supply more input or mark end-of-input.
  • Review snapshots, signatures and cache keys that depend on encoded bytes. Source and attribute-only methods are unchanged.

Public APIs, Java 8 support, runtime dependencies and module/bundle identities are unchanged. No new encoder security fix is introduced. The 1.5.0 protections remain; users of older versions should follow the security advisory. See the migration record.

Maven Central

Version 1.6.0 is published under org.owasp.encoder:

  • encoder
  • encoder-jsp
  • encoder-jakarta-jsp
  • encoder-parent

Keep core and adapter versions aligned. Do not combine javax and Jakarta adapters. The retired ESAPI adapter and optional test WAR are not included. Javadoc JARs are attached; hosted javadoc.io indexing can lag publication.

title: maven(deps): bump org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on from 1.85 to 1.86
body:
Bumps [org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on](https://github.com/bcgit/bc-java) from 1.85 to 1.86.
Changelog

Sourced from org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on's changelog.

Bouncy Castle Crypto Package - Release Notes

1.0 Introduction

The Bouncy Castle Crypto package is a Java implementation of cryptographic algorithms. The package is organised so that it contains a light-weight API suitable for use in any environment (including the J2ME) with the additional infrastructure to conform the algorithms to the JCE framework.

2.0 Release History

2.1.1 Version

Release: 1.87
Date: 2026, TBD

2.1.2 Defects Fixed

  • A PBEKey stored in a BCFKS KeyStore was not reported as a key entry: isKeyEntry() returned false for it, so KeyStore.getEntry() returned null rather than a SecretKeyEntry, although getKey() recovered it. The PBE key entry type added for github #2164 was missing from engineIsKeyEntry, and is now included.

  • The CMS content-type decoders SignedData, EnvelopedData, AuthenticatedData, AuthEnvelopedData and EncryptedData read their mandatory fields by index or enumeration with no lower-bound size check, so a ContentInfo whose inner content was an empty or too-short SEQUENCE - malformed but DER-parseable - left the decode as an unchecked NoSuchElementException or ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than the CMSException the CMSSignedData, CMSEnvelopedData, CMSAuthenticatedData and CMSAuthEnvelopedData constructors declare (the IllegalArgumentException CMSEncryptedData documents). Each now rejects a short sequence with IllegalArgumentException before reading, as the sibling content types CompressedData and DigestedData already did, so the wrappers surface it as their declared exception; the case that claims an OPTIONAL field and then truncates the mandatory ones after it is covered too. The streaming parsers CMSSignedDataParser, CMSEnvelopedDataParser, CMSAuthenticatedDataParser, CMSAuthEnvelopedDataParser and CMSCompressedDataParser had the same gap and more: an absent or truncated inner SEQUENCE, a mandatory field of the wrong type, or absent encapsulated or encrypted content escaped as NullPointerException, ClassCastException, IllegalArgumentException or IllegalStateException. The asn1.cms stream parsers now report a missing mandatory field as an IOException, and the CMS parsers report malformed content as CMSException ("Malformed content." / "Missing content.") or the IOException they declare.

  • A KeyAgreement asked for its shared secret before doPhase returned data rather than refusing. javax.crypto.KeyAgreement specifies IllegalStateException for that state, but nothing in the provider tracked it, so each SPI handed back whatever its result field held: for Diffie-Hellman that was the private value itself - engineInit seeded result with x, so generateSecret() returned the private exponent padded to the prime's length and generateSecret("AES") an all-zero key taken from that padding - while ECDH returned null and its named-algorithm overload raised NullPointerException. BaseAgreementSpi now records whether a doPhase has completed the agreement since the last init and refuses the request with an IllegalStateException naming the algorithm, so every family in the provider - DH, ECDH and ECMQV, the SM2 exchange, both ECGOST families, XDH, SM9 and NewHope - answers the same way, and the DH SPI no longer holds the private value in that field at all.

title: github-actions(deps): bump github/codeql-action from 4.38.3 to 4.39.0
body:
Bumps [github/codeql-action](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) from 4.38.3 to 4.39.0.
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action's releases.

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

body:
Bumps [org.owasp.encoder:encoder](https://github.com/OWASP/owasp-java-encoder) from 1.5.0 to 1.5.1.
Release notes

Sourced from org.owasp.encoder:encoder's releases.

OWASP Java Encoder 1.5.1 is a documentation and build-maintenance patch. Encoding behavior, public APIs, runtime dependencies, and Java 8 support are unchanged from 1.5.0.

What changed

  • Clarify JavaScript encoding modes, output growth, and where encoded values can safely be inserted.
  • Explain why script-letter escapes remain necessary in the general and block modes; Source mode already leaves the URL in #243 unchanged.
  • Distinguish JSON whole-string HTML embedding from JavaScript fragment protection, with clearer surrounding-template requirements.
  • Strengthen parser regression tests and include the build/test maintenance recorded in CHANGELOG.md.

The documentation changes are in #244. The release preparation is in #245. This patch preserves the security fixes from 1.5.0 and introduces no new encoder security fix. Users upgrading from versions older than 1.5.0 should read the 1.5.0 migration notes and security advisory.

Maven Central

Version 1.5.1 is published under org.owasp.encoder:

  • encoder
  • encoder-jsp
  • encoder-jakarta-jsp
  • encoder-parent

Keep core and adapter versions aligned. The retired ESAPI adapter and optional Jakarta test WAR are not included. The Javadoc JARs are attached. Hosted core, JSP, and Jakarta documentation is live and was checked against the released Javadoc content.

title: TRUNK-6839: Stop startup if anything is mounted into the folders rebuilt from the distribution
body:
## Description of what I changed

Since TRUNK-6508, `startup-init.sh` removes and recreates the data directory's `modules/`, `owa/`, `configuration/` and `frontend/` on every start, then copies the distribution in. When one of these is a bind mount, `rm -fR` deletes the host's files first and then fails on the mount point itself ("Resource busy"), so startup stops under `set -e`. A file mounted into one of them (e.g. a single `.omod` in `modules/`) also stops startup.

Startup now checks `/proc/self/mountinfo` before deleting anything. If one of these folders is, or contains, a mount point, it stops with an error that names the matching `/openmrs/distribution` folder to mount into instead, e.g.:

```
Error: /openmrs/data/modules is, or contains, a mount point. It is rebuilt from /openmrs/distribution/openmrs_modules on every start, so mount into /openmrs/distribution/openmrs_modules instead.
```

**Rationale:** these folders are output, rebuilt from the distribution on every start, so anything mounted into them would either be deleted or would conflict with that. Rather than special-casing mounts (skipping folders, deleting around mount points, handling read-only targets), the script refuses them and points at the place that already supports it: `/openmrs/distribution` is copied in on every start, so files mounted there work as expected. Everything else is unchanged.

**Behaviour change:** a setup that mounts into one of these folders now fails at startup with the message above, instead of losing the host's files (or, on releases without TRUNK-6508, silently mixing them with the distribution's).

Not changed:
- Files placed by hand in these folders on a `/openmrs/data` volume (as the O3 configuration docs currently describe) are still removed on restart. The docs will be updated to point at `/openmrs/distribution`, as described on TRUNK-6839.
- `OMRS_HOME` containing a space already makes `startup-init.sh` fail at the server properties redirect, on master too. That's separate.

Raised in review of #6695, which will include this when it's backported to 2.8.x.

## Testing

Ran the whole `startup-init.sh` under `bash -aeu` in containers (bash 4.2, bash 5.3 with busybox awk, Debian with mawk), with stale files in each folder and a module and config in the distribution:

| Mounts | Result |
|---|---|
| none | folders cleared, only the distribution's files remain |
| host folder bind-mounted on `modules/` | stops with the error; nothing deleted, host files kept |
| single `.omod` mounted into `modules/` | stops with the error; nothing deleted |
| `configuration/addresshierarchy/` mounted | stops with the error; nothing deleted |
| `configuration/` mounted read-only | stops with the error |
| whole `/openmrs/data` as one volume | folders cleared as before |
| sibling mount on `data/modules2` | `modules/` cleared as before |
| single `.omod` mounted into `/openmrs/distribution/openmrs_modules/` | copied into `modules/` with the distribution's |
| `/proc/self/mountinfo` unreadable | stops before deleting anything |

No new variables or functions are left in the environment Tomcat inherits. I have not built the image.

title: TRUNK-6832: Apply explicitly set DB connection settings to an existing runtime properties file
body:
> **Depends on #6687** (uses its `escape_property`, and changes the same merge block). Based on that branch so only this commit shows; it will retarget to master once #6687 is merged.

## Description of what I changed

`startup-init.sh` writes the DB connection settings (`OMRS_DB_*`, and the deprecated `OMRS_CONFIG_CONNECTION_*`) only into the installation properties, which OpenMRS reads only on first install. On later starts only `OMRS_EXTRA_*` and `admin.password.locked` reach the existing runtime properties file, so a changed DB password, user or URL in the environment never reaches an existing instance. After a password rotation OpenMRS keeps the old one and fails to connect, with nothing in the log pointing at the cause.

On each start with an existing runtime properties file, `connection.username`, `connection.password`, `connection.url` and `connection.driver_class` are now written into it from the environment:

- Only for settings **set explicitly**. Anything left to the image's defaults keeps the file's value, so instances that don't set these variables are unaffected.
- `connection.url` is rewritten when `OMRS_DB_URL` or any setting it is built from (`OMRS_DB`, `OMRS_DB_HOSTNAME`, `_PORT`, `_NAME`, `_ARGS`, `_EXTRA_ARGS`, `_JDBC_PROTOCOL`, or their `OMRS_CONFIG_*` names) is set. For an instance installed by the image, the rebuilt URL is the one already in the file: the default arguments are the same on 2.7.x through master, and the installer writes the URL unchanged.
- `connection.driver_class` is written whenever `connection.url` is (its protocol depends on `OMRS_DB`), or when `OMRS_DB_DRIVER_CLASS` is set.
- Keys are matched as Java parses them (`key = value`, `key:value`, continuation lines), and only entries for the keys being set are replaced. Other entries in the runtime file, including duplicates added by hand, are left as they are.
- `OMRS_EXTRA_CONNECTION_*` still takes precedence, as it does on first install.
- Values are escaped for the properties format (#6687), and the log names the keys updated, not their values.

**Rationale:** the environment is where these settings are configured, so it should be the source of truth on every start, not only the first. The alternative, documenting `OMRS_EXTRA_CONNECTION_*` for changes after install, already works but means setting the same secret in two variables.

**Behaviour change:** if these variables are set but the runtime file has since been edited by hand (e.g. a different password or URL parameters), the environment now wins on the next start. If anyone relies on the current behaviour, please say so here or on TRUNK-6832.

**Behaviour change (admin password lock):** the existing `admin.password.locked` merge uses the same key matching. Before, a hand-edited `admin.password.locked = false` (spaced, or with `:`) wasn't recognised as the same key, so it beat `OMRS_ADMIN_PASSWORD_LOCKED`. Now the environment wins, as it already did for the exact `admin.password.locked=` spelling. This applies on every start of an existing instance, whether or not any DB variables are set.

## Testing

Ran the whole `startup-init.sh` under `bash -aeu` against a temporary `OMRS_HOME`, with an existing runtime properties file written by `java.util.Properties.store` (as OpenMRS writes it), then read it back with `java.util.Properties`:

| Environment | Result |
|---|---|
| `OMRS_CONFIG_CONNECTION_SERVER/DATABASE/USERNAME/PASSWORD` (password changed, containing `\`) | password updated exactly; username and URL rewritten with the same values; other keys kept |
| nothing DB-related set | file unchanged |
| only `OMRS_DB_PASSWORD` | only `connection.password` updated |
| `OMRS_DB_PASSWORD` and `OMRS_EXTRA_connection_password` | the extra property wins |
| first install (no runtime file) | unchanged behaviour |
| installed as mysql, restarted with `OMRS_DB=mariadb` | URL and driver class both switch to MariaDB |
| only `OMRS_DB_DRIVER_CLASS` | only `connection.driver_class` updated |

title: TRUNK-6834: Write JAVA_OPTS and CATALINA_OPTS into setenv.sh quoted
body:
## Description of what I changed

`startup.sh` wrote `JAVA_OPTS` and `CATALINA_OPTS` into Tomcat's `setenv.sh` inside double quotes. `catalina.sh` (Tomcat 9 and 11) sources `setenv.sh` and then starts Java with `eval exec ... "$JAVA_OPTS" "$CATALINA_OPTS"`, so every option was interpreted by the shell twice: `$` was expanded, a `"` broke `setenv.sh`, `&` backgrounded Java, and quoting in `OMRS_JAVA_SERVER_OPTS` couldn't protect anything.

The values are now written single-quoted, so the `eval` is the only interpretation, as Tomcat documents for `JAVA_OPTS`. A value with special characters can be quoted in the variable, e.g. `-Dkey='a$b&c'`. Single quotes rather than `printf %q`, because `catalina.sh` runs under `/bin/sh` (dash), which can't read the `$'...'` form bash produces for some values.

**Behaviour change:** plain options and `$CATALINA_HOME`-style references work as before. Only a value escaped twice to work around the old behaviour (e.g. `\"a b\"` for a space) now reaches Java differently.

## Testing

Ran the new `setenv.sh`-writing code under `bash -aeu`, then a stand-in for `catalina.sh` under dash that sources `setenv.sh` and runs Tomcat's `eval exec` line, printing the arguments Java would get:

| `OMRS_JAVA_SERVER_OPTS` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `-Dtest.value='a$HOMEb'` | `a` | `a$HOMEb` |
| `-Dtest.quote='x"y'` | `setenv.sh` syntax error | `x"y` |
| `-Dtest.space="a b"` | `a` | `a b` |
| `-Dtest.sq="it's"` | — | `it's` |
| `-Dtest.home=$CATALINA_HOME/x` | expanded | expanded |
| the default options | unchanged | unchanged |

title: TRUNK-6836: ProgramValidator evicts the program being saved, so saving a program from the session fails on Hibernate 7
body:
## Description of what I changed

`ProgramValidator.validate` evicted the program it found by name whenever that program had the same uuid. When the program being saved is already in the session, `getProgramByName` returns that same instance. The validator runs from `RequiredDataAdvice` before the DAO, so it evicted the very program being saved, with its workflows. `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate` then merged a detached graph. On Hibernate 7, that merge either inserts a workflow flushed earlier a second time (a duplicate uuid in `program_workflow`) or throws an NPE in `StatefulPersistenceContext.replaceCollection`.

The eviction is removed. `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate` merges a detached program, so a loaded copy in the session no longer gets in the way.

Two new tests in `ProgramWorkflowServiceTest` fail on master and pass with this change. `saveProgram_shouldAddAWorkflowToAProgramWhoseNewWorkflowWasAlreadyFlushed` fails with the duplicate-uuid insert. `saveProgram_shouldUpdateProgramCreatedEarlierInTheSameSession`, moved here from #6639, saves a new program a second time before anything is flushed and fails with the NPE. `saveProgram_shouldUpdateDetachedProgram` still passes.

This also fixes the two failing loader tests in the Initializer module's Platform 3.0 upgrade (mekomsolutions/openmrs-module-initializer#338): `ProgramWorkflowsLoaderIntegrationTest` and `ProgramWorkflowStatesLoaderIntegrationTest`. Against a core built from this branch, Initializer's suite passes, with 220 tests and 0 failures.

title: maven(deps): bump org.postgresql:postgresql from 42.7.13 to 42.7.14
body:
Bumps [org.postgresql:postgresql](https://github.com/pgjdbc/pgjdbc) from 42.7.13 to 42.7.14.
Release notes

Sourced from org.postgresql:postgresql's releases.

v42.7.14

Security

This release fixes two security vulnerabilities.

requireAuth is silently not enforced when the value excludes every authentication method (GHSA-rhp9-mr79-r74h, CVE-2026-107314)

Severity: Moderate (CVSS 5.9) | Affected versions: 42.7.11 – 42.7.13

If the requireAuth connection property excluded all six authentication methods the driver knows (for example requireAuth=!password,!md5,!gss,!sspi,!scram-sha-256,!none) or contained no method at all (for example requireAuth=,), the driver applied no restriction and accepted whatever method the server asked for, including cleartext password. An attacker positioned between the application and the server could use this to request cleartext password authentication and receive the database password.

Unset values, positive lists (such as requireAuth=scram-sha-256) and partial exclusions (such as requireAuth=!password,!md5) were not affected, and neither were deployments that do not set requireAuth.

Behavior after upgrading:

  • A value that excludes every method now refuses the connection with SQLState 08004 and the message Authentication method is not allowed by requireAuth (or the channel binding error when channelBinding=require is also set).
  • A value that names no method is rejected as an invalid requireAuth value.

Because affected deployments had this value by mistake, and connections worked normally on affected versions, connections with such a value will fail after upgrading. Replace it with a positive list of the methods your server uses, for example requireAuth=scram-sha-256.

Independently of this fix, use sslmode=verify-full with a trusted CA so that an attacker cannot present a substitute server.

Thanks to @​manus-pi for finding and reporting this issue.

Driver stores bytes of earlier statements when it pads a value shorter than its declared length (GHSA-f64h-wr5q-3qf3, CVE-2026-107315)

Severity: Moderate (CVSS 5.3) | Affected versions: 42.7.4 – 42.7.13

When an application sent a value shorter than the length it declared, the driver padded the missing bytes with data from earlier messages on the same connection instead of zeros, and the server stored them. The stored value could contain SQL text and parameter values of earlier, unrelated statements (up to 8192 bytes, or 16320 with GSS encryption). On pooled connections, those statements could come from other requests. 42.7.3 and earlier padded with zeros.

This is reachable through the following public API when the declared length is larger than the data:

  • PreparedStatement.setObject(int, ByteStreamWriter)
  • CopyIn.writeToCopy(ByteStreamWriter) and CopyIn.writeToCopy(byte[], int, int)
  • PGCopyOutputStream.write(byte[], int, int) (writes over 64 KiB)
  • LargeObject.write(byte[], int, int)

title: TRUNK-6829: Fix case, duplicates, backslashes and escaping in properties written by startup-init.sh
body:
## Description of what I changed

Four fixes to how `startup-init.sh` writes runtime and server properties, one commit per ticket. They change the same few lines, so they are reviewed and backported together.

- **TRUNK-6829:** `OMRS_EXTRA_*` names containing any lower case letter keep their case (e.g. `OMRS_EXTRA_mail_smtp_socketFactory_class` → `mail.smtp.socketFactory.class`). All upper case names are lowercased as before. Also replaces the unquoted `tr [:upper:] [:lower:]`, whose arguments were subject to pathname expansion: with a one-character file such as `u` or `e` in the working directory, no extra properties were written.
- **TRUNK-6830:** when several `OMRS_EXTRA_*` variables give the same property, the first in sorted order is used and the others are logged and ignored. Previously the last won on first install and the first on later starts.
- **TRUNK-6831:** extra properties are written with `printf` instead of `echo -e`, so backslash sequences in values are no longer interpreted (differently on each path).
- **TRUNK-6835:** values written to the server and runtime properties files are escaped for the Java properties format (`\`, line breaks, leading whitespace). A backslash in `OMRS_DB_PASSWORD`, for example, now reaches OpenMRS unchanged.

**Behaviour changes:**
- A mixed-case name that relied on being lowercased now keeps its case, e.g. `OMRS_EXTRA_Initializer_DOMAINS` used to set `initializer.domains` and now sets `Initializer.DOMAINS`. Such names need to be written all upper case, or in the property's exact case.
- Anyone who escaped backslashes in these variables by hand to work around the old handling will now get doubled backslashes.

**Not covered:** non-ASCII values. The install script is read with `Properties.load(InputStream)` (ISO-8859-1) and runtime properties as UTF-8.

## Testing

No automated tests cover `startup-init.sh`. I ran the properties section of the script under `bash -aeu` for both a first install and an existing runtime properties file, and loaded the output with `java.util.Properties` as OpenMRS does:

- On `master`, each of the four problems reproduces.
- On this branch, a value containing `\t`, `\\`, `=`, `:`, `#`, leading spaces, CR and LF, and a DB password containing `\`, read back exactly as set on both paths. Mixed-case and duplicate names behave as described above.

I have not built the image or started a container with it. The four commits cherry-pick cleanly onto 2.9.x and 2.8.x.

see https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/TRUNK-6829, https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/TRUNK-6830, https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/TRUNK-6831, https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/TRUNK-6835

title: TRUNK-6809: Run the Liquibase status check inside the update scope (2.9.x)
body:
## Description of what I changed

Backport of #6679 to `2.9.x`. The master commit doesn't apply cleanly, so this cherry-picks the `2.8.x` backport (#6685), which applies without conflicts. Authorship is kept with the original author.

`DatabaseUpdater.executeChangelog` counted the unrun changesets before entering the Liquibase scope that installs OpenMRS's composite resource accessor. For an already-run `runOnChange` changeset, Liquibase's status check recomputes the checksum and reads files such as `<sqlFile>` through the current scope's accessor. Outside the OpenMRS scope, module files aren't found and module startup fails.

- `executeChangelog`: count the changesets inside the existing scope (after the lock).
- `getUnrunDatabaseChanges`: run its status check in a `Scope.child` with the same resource accessor.

## Verification on 2.9.x

- `DatabaseUpdaterTest`: 8/8 pass with the change. On unpatched `2.9.x` the two new tests fail with `UnexpectedLiquibaseException: Resource does not exist`.
- The end-to-end before/after (Bahmni Appointments failing to start on a restored long-running server's database, then starting cleanly with the fix on a first and a second run) was done on `2.8.x`; see #6685.

title: TRUNK-6827: Keep the outbox from enqueueing events about its own rows (2.9.x backport)
body:
Backport of the outbox part of #6637 ([TRUNK-6827](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/TRUNK-6827)).

On 2.9.x, `EventInterceptor.onSave` runs for every insert, so saving an `OutboxEvent` publishes a `SaveDbEvent` about it. An `@OutboxEventListener` that accepts that event (one taking `SaveDbEvent<?>` or `EntityEvent<?>`, say) then makes `OutboxEventInterceptor` save another `OutboxEvent`, and so on until the heap runs out on the first create or update. `OutboxEventInterceptor` now ignores entity events about an `OutboxEvent`.

The rest of #6637 isn't needed here. Hibernate 5.6 calls `onSave` and `onDelete`, which this branch's `EventInterceptor` overrides, so create and delete events already reach it. `OutboxEvent` isn't `@Audited` on 2.9.x, so its Envers audit rows can't feed the loop either.

**Tests:**
- `OutboxEventInterceptorTest` is the same as on master. Without the check, the test that keeps events about an `OutboxEvent` out of the outbox fails.
- The api suite passes: 5485 tests, 0 failures.
- I also ran a temporary context-sensitive test with Envers on, an `@OutboxEventListener` taking `EntityEvent<?>`, and real commits. Without the check, creating a location, a patient or a global property runs out of heap. With it, each one commits and adds a handful of outbox rows (five for a location).

title: TRUNK-6826: Request paths with a trailing slash find no handler on core 3.0
body:
## Description of what I changed

On core 3.0, `/openmrs/ws/rest/v1/session/` no longer reaches the handler for `/openmrs/ws/rest/v1/session`. A 2.x server (platform 2.9.0-SNAPSHOT, Spring 5.3.30) answers both with 200. Spring 7 has no option to match a handler mapping to a path with a trailing slash; in spring-webmvc/spring-web 7.0.9, `PathMatchConfigurer`, `RequestMappingHandlerMapping` and `PathPatternParser` have no trailing-slash member, while 6.2.12's `PathPatternParser` still has `setMatchOptionalTrailingSeparator`.

With the RefApp module set the missing handler shows up as a 500 rather than a 404: webservices.rest maps `/rest/**` to `unknownResourceController` through a `SimpleUrlHandlerMapping`, and no handler adapter supports that `@Controller` (`ServletException: No adapter for handler [...UnknownResourceController...]`). `/ws/rest/nosuch` answers the same 500 without any trailing slash, so that part belongs to the REST module and is not changed here.

`TrailingSlashFilter` hands a `/ws` request whose path ends in `/` to Spring's `UrlHandlerFilter`, which trims the slash from the request URI, URL and path info. It passes on unchanged:
- requests the container mapped to any other servlet,
- `/openmrs/ws/` itself, where legacyui serves its index page (`UrlHandlerFilter` leaves the servlet root alone),
- a request URI that does not start with the context path and `/ws/`, such as `/openmrs//ws/x/`, which `UrlHandlerFilter` cannot parse,
- a request URI ending in `//`. `UrlHandlerFilter` trims one slash, which would leave the URI ending in a single `/` that the firewall no longer rejects. Passed on unchanged, it gets the firewall's 400, as on master.

`web.xml` maps it right after `charsetFilter`, ahead of `springSecurityFilterChain` as `UrlHandlerFilter`'s javadoc asks, and so ahead of `openmrsAuthorizationFilter`. An `AuthorizedUrlMatcher` rule therefore judges the path the handler is chosen on: an exact rule on `/secure/x` still challenges `/ws/secure/x/`.

Tests:
- `TrailingSlashFilterTest`: URI, URL and path info trimmed with the query string kept, in a `/openmrs` and a root deployment; requests left alone without a trailing slash, at the `/ws` root, without path info, to another servlet, with `//` after the context path, with a URI ending in `//`, and with a dot segment that the container mapped to `/scripts`.
- `WebSecurityConfigIntegrationTest`: with the filter ahead of the real `springSecurityFilterChain` and `openmrsAuthorizationFilter`, `/openmrs/ws/public/x/` reaches the `/public/x` handler (404 without the filter), an anonymous `/openmrs/ws/secure/x/` gets 401 from the exact `/secure/x` rule (200 if the filter runs after `openmrsAuthorizationFilter`), and `/openmrs/ws/public/x//`, shaped the way Tomcat delivers it, gets the firewall's 400 (404 without the `//` check).

Checked under `jetty:run` with all 31 O3 modules on a fresh MySQL database, master at ee18bf341b and this branch at its head:

| Request | master | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/ws/rest/v1/session/`, `/ws/rest/v1/location/`, `/ws/rest/v1/location/?v=full` | 500 | 200, same as without the slash |
| `/ws/rest/v1/patient/` | 500 | 400, same as without the slash |
| `/ws/rest/v1/nosuchthing/` | 500 | 404 from REST, same as without the slash |
| `/ws/index.htm/` | 404 | 200, same as without the slash |
| POST to `/ws/rest/v1/location/` | not measured | 201 |
| `/ws/fhir2/R4/metadata/`, `/ws/fhir2/R4/Patient/` | 200 | 200, same as without the slash |
| `/ws/` | 200 (legacyui index) | 200 (legacyui index) |
| anonymous `/ws/admin/index.htm/` | not measured | 302 to login, same as without the slash |

Jetty answers any URI with `//` with 400 before the application sees it, so the `//` cases were not run on a server.

If #6673 (TRUNK-6824) also merges, both PRs add a filter at the same place in `web.xml`, and `RepeatedSlashFilter` has to come first. In the other order, on Tomcat, `/openmrs//ws/rest/v1/session/` and `/openmrs/ws/rest/v1/session

title: TRUNK-6809: Run the Liquibase status check inside the update scope
body:
## Description of what I changed

`DatabaseUpdater.executeChangelog` counted the unrun changesets (`StatusCommandStep.listUnrunChangeSets`) *before* entering the Liquibase scope that installs OpenMRS's composite resource accessor (classpath + application data directory, TRUNK-6295). For a changeset that has already run and is `runOnChange="true"`, Liquibase's status check recomputes the checksum (`ShouldRunChangeSetFilter`), and that reads files such as `<sqlFile>` through the current scope's resource accessor (`SQLFileChange.getResource`). Outside the OpenMRS scope that is the thread's root classloader accessor, so a module's sql file isn't found and module startup fails, as Mike saw with Bahmni appointments on 2.8.9.

- `executeChangelog`: count the changesets inside the existing scope (after the lock).
- `getUnrunDatabaseChanges`: run its status check in a `Scope.child` with the same resource accessor.

| Check | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| `executeChangelog` second run of a `runOnChange` `<sqlFile>` changeset | fails in `StatusCommandStep.listUnrunChangeSets` ("Resource does not exist") | passes |
| `getUnrunDatabaseChanges` on the same changelog | fails, same cause | passes (nothing left to run) |

The two new tests put the changelog and sql file in the application data directory, which only OpenMRS's composite accessor sees. That reproduces the module case without a real module. Both fail with only the main change reverted.

Note for a 2.8.x backport: the commit doesn't cherry-pick cleanly onto `2.8.x` (conflicts in `DatabaseUpdater` and its test), so it would need a small manual port.

title: TRUNK-6823: Deny with APIAuthenticationException again, as an AuthorizationDeniedException
body:
## Description of what I changed

Since TRUNK-6799, `AuthorizationAdvice` and core's explicit privilege checks deny with Spring Security's `AccessDeniedException` instead of `APIAuthenticationException`. Code that catches the old type no longer sees these denials. webservices.rest maps only that type, so REST now answers 500 where it answered 401 or 403.

This keeps `AccessDeniedException` as the type a denial is. It only makes the deprecated exception a subtype of it:

- `APIAuthenticationException` now extends `AuthorizationDeniedException`. Its constructors keep their messages and causes, and it gains one that takes an `AuthorizationResult`. It stays `@Deprecated`, pointing new code at `AccessDeniedException`.
- `@Authorized` denies with it again (`AuthorizationAdvice`'s three throw sites), and so do the checks #6544 had switched to `AccessDeniedException`: `Daemon.runInNewDaemonThread`/`runNewDaemonTask`, `UserContext.becomeUser`, `AlertServiceImpl.getAlerts` and `TestInstallUtil.getResourceInputStream`.
- `PrivilegeNamingAuthorizationManager` returns it as the result when a `@PreAuthorize`/`@PostAuthorize` check names the missing privilege, and when `isAuthenticated()` denies a caller who is not logged in. The second case carries "Basic authentication required", as `@Authorized()` does. Spring's default handler throws that result, so converting a method by the guide's translation table keeps what its callers catch. Only an expression that names neither, such as `denyAll()`, still denies with a plain `AuthorizationDeniedException`. URL rules are unchanged.
- `doc/AUTHORIZATION_MIGRATION.md`, `ExceptionUtil` and the exception's javadoc say so. The guide has a Pitfalls row for the `VerifyError` below.

webservices.rest still needs RESTWS-1056 (openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest#767) for denials that are not an `APIAuthenticationException`.

**Compatibility.** `APIAuthenticationException` is no longer an `APIException`.

- **Compiled bytecode that treats it as one fails JVM verification.** A module built against an earlier core breaks until it is rebuilt.
- **Example: patientdocuments.** It has `catch (APIAuthenticationException | ContextAuthenticationException e)` in two controllers, which javac types as `APIException`. Its omod as built today, against core master, stops this branch's OpenMRS from starting: `VerifyError` while Spring maps `VisitSummaryPreviewController`. Rebuilt against this branch with no source change, it starts and works.
- **After this merges,** patientdocuments' 3.0 SNAPSHOT needs a rebuild before a server running it will start, as does any other module whose bytecode has that shape.
- **Scan of the RefApp 3.0 module builds:** 19 classes in the 29 module builds reference the exception. Only those two handlers have this bytecode shape, though other shapes are possible.
- **Source compatibility:** code that assigns it to an `APIException` stops compiling. `catch (APIException e)` no longer catches a denial core throws, which is already the case on master. After this change it also misses an `APIAuthenticationException` a module throws itself. 6 of the 29 RefApp 3.0 module builds throw one, and none of their catches relies on catching it as an `APIException`.
- **A catch naming both types stops compiling.** That covers `catch (AccessDeniedException | APIAuthenticationException e)`, and `catch (AccessDeniedException)` followed by `catch (APIAuthenticationException)`. Catch `AccessDeniedException` alone, which covers both before and after this change. openmrs/openmrs-module-legacyui#272 has four such catches, and openmrs/openmrs-module-legacyui#274 has two in `DWRAdministrationServiceTest`.

Verified on core 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT with the RefApp 3.0 modules and the published webservices.rest 5.0.0-SNAPSHOT, using `GET /ws/rest/v1/patient?q=Anderson&v=default`:

| Caller | build 435 (master) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| No credentials | 500 `AuthorizationDeniedException` | 401 "User is not logged in [Privile

title: TRUNK-6824: Request paths with a repeated slash fail with 500 on core 3.0
body:
## Description of what I changed

On core master, `GET /openmrs//ws/rest/v1/session` answers 500:

```
IllegalArgumentException: Invalid contextPath '/openmrs/ws': must match the start of requestPath: '/openmrs//ws/rest/v1/session'
    at org.springframework.web.util.ServletRequestPathUtils.parseAndCache(ServletRequestPathUtils.java:70)
    at org.springframework.web.filter.ServletRequestPathFilter.doFilter(ServletRequestPathFilter.java:50)
    at org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.configuration.WebSecurityConfiguration$CompositeFilterChainProxy.doFilter(WebSecurityConfiguration.java:317)
    at org.openmrs.web.security.RefreshableDelegatingFilterProxy.doFilter(RefreshableDelegatingFilterProxy.java:84)
```

Tomcat normalizes the servlet path and path info, but `getRequestURI()` keeps the slashes the client sent. Spring Security's composite runs `ServletRequestPathFilter` ahead of `FilterChainProxy`, and its parse needs the context path plus the servlet path to start that URI. So a repeated slash at or before `/ws` fails there with a 500, before the firewall can answer the 400 it gives a `//` further in. The O3 patient chart's visit history requests `/openmrs//ws/rest/v1/visit`, which 2.x served, so the Visits dashboard shows "Error 500" on a 3.0 backend.

`RepeatedSlashFilter`, mapped right after `charsetFilter` in `web.xml`, collapses each run of slashes in the request URI, URL and context path. Everything downstream (Spring's path parsing, `springSecurityFilterChain`, `ModuleFilter`, CSRFGuard and `OpenmrsAuthorizationFilter`) then sees the path the container dispatched on. Requests without `//` pass through unwrapped.

`WebSecurityConfig`'s javadoc keeps `StrictHttpFirewall` at its defaults because a URL rule matches the request URI rather than the dispatched path. After this filter the two agree about repeated slashes, so `//admin/x` is still challenged by an `/admin/**` rule. The firewall settings are unchanged, and `filterChain_shouldRejectAUrlShapeThatCouldWalkAroundAUrlRule`, which sends `//` to the chain directly, still expects 400. The filter changes nothing but repeated slashes. `/openmrs/ws;x=y/rest/v1/session` and `/openmrs/x/../ws/rest/v1/session` still fail with a 500 in `ServletRequestPathFilter`, as on master, and Tomcat itself refuses an encoded slash with 400.

Tests:
- `RepeatedSlashFilterTest` covers the URI, URL and context path shapes Tomcat produces, and leaves the query string and `%2F` alone. It also shows `ServletRequestPathUtils.parseAndCache` failing on the raw request and succeeding on the filtered one.
- `WebSecurityConfigIntegrationTest` runs the filter ahead of the real chain. Guarded URLs reached through `//` (including `/openmrs//ws/admin/x`) get 401, and public ones get 200. Without the filter these get 400 from the firewall, or, where the repeated slash sits at or before the `/ws` servlet path, the `ServletRequestPathFilter` exception.
- `WebXmlTest` (webapp module) reads `web.xml` and requires a `RepeatedSlashFilter` mapping on `/*` for requests, ahead of `springSecurityFilterChain`'s. It fails if those lines are deleted, moved below the security chain, or narrowed.

Checked by hand on Tomcat 11 with this war and the RefApp module set on 3.0:

| Request | master | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/openmrs//ws/rest/v1/session`, `//openmrs/ws/...`, `/openmrs///ws/...` | 500 | 200 |
| `/openmrs/ws//rest/v1/session`, `/openmrs//login.htm` | 400 | 200 |
| The O3 visit-history URL above | 500 | 200, same body as with one slash |
| Anonymous `//ws/fhir2/R4/Patient`, `//admin/index.htm`, token-less POST to `//admin/users/user.form` | not measured | 401, 302 to login, 302 to `error.html` (same as with one slash) |
| `/openmrs/ws/rest/v1/%2F%2Fsession` | 400 | 400 |

The RefApp 3.7.1 Visits dashboard lists the patient's visits again instead of "Error 500".

A trailing `//` now collapses to a single trailing slash. Core 3.0 answers that with a 500 whether or not this change is in

title: Read the name layout global properties with a proxy privilege
body:
Fixes #6669.

`NameSupport` now reads `layout.name.template` and `layout.name.format` with "Get Global Properties" added as a proxy privilege, the way `OpenmrsConfigurationFactory`, `OpenmrsLoggingUtil` and `OpenmrsPropertyLookup` read theirs. Formatting a name no longer depends on whether the viewer may read global properties, so `PersonName.getFullName()` and `Provider.getName()` work for every user again, and they use the configured layout.

I didn't catch `AccessDeniedException` in `getFullName()` instead, next to `APIException`. That would restore 2.x's behaviour, where a user without the privilege gets the built-in format rather than the configured one. Until a privileged user initializes `NameSupport`, each of that user's calls would also retry `init()`, which registers the global property listener again.

**Tests**
- New: `NameTemplateTest.shouldUseNameTemplateConfiguredViaGlobalPropertiesForAUserWithoutGetGlobalProperties`. It configures a template through the global properties, resets `NameSupport` so that it initializes as a user with no roles, and calls `getFullName()` as that user.
  - On master it fails with the `AuthorizationDeniedException` from #6669, in `NameSupport.init`.
  - Reverting either read to a plain `getGlobalProperty` call fails it again, at `init` or at `getDefaultLayoutFormat`.
- The full default api suite passes: 5605 tests, 0 failures.

**Runtime:** Bahmni/openmrs-module-appointments#213's `AppointmentsServiceTest.shouldFetchAppointments` fails on build 435 at `provider.getName()`. Built against this and #6672, the module's api tests pass, in a Linux container and on a Mac.

title: TRUNK-6820: Write the DWR document type when creating dwr-modules.xml
body:
## Description of what I changed

`WebModuleUtil` tags each module's entries in `dwr-modules.xml` with a `moduleId` attribute so they can be removed when the module stops, and DWR validates the file against a DTD that did not declare it, so every startup with legacyui logged:

```
ERROR - CommonsLoggingOutput.error(75) | Line=4 Attribute "moduleId" must be declared for element type "allow".
ERROR - CommonsLoggingOutput.error(75) | Line=384 Attribute "moduleId" must be declared for element type "signatures".
```

That is fixed in the DTD itself, which legacyui's DWR resolves from openmrs-contrib-dwr: https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-dwr/pull/7 declares `moduleId` and lets the file hold the entries of any number of modules. The second part also clears `The content of element type "dwr" must match "(init?,allow?,signatures?)"`, which a second module with dwr config (htmlformentry, atlas, appointmentscheduling, reportingcompatibility) triggers and which an internal subset in this file could not fix.

What remains in core: `createDwrModulesXml`, which `startModule` and `stopModule` use when the file is missing, wrote no document type at all, so DWR had no grammar to validate the file against, and `Listener` kept the file that way on every restart. It now writes the same document type `Listener` writes.

title: TRUNK-6819: Start the JobRunr job server only once OpenMRS has started
body:
## Description of what I changed

Running the webapp with `mvn jetty:run` and modules installed logged job failures during startup, because the JobRunr background job server started while its application context was still being created:

- `IllegalStateException: EntityManagerFactory is closed`: a job ran during the context refresh that follows module startup, against the closed session factory of the context being replaced.
- `TaskException: Task class org.openmrs.module.stockmanagement.api.jobs.AsyncTasksBatchJob not found`: a module's job ran right after the first, core-only refresh, before modules were loaded.

The server is now created with `startBackgroundJobServer = false` and driven by a new `JobRunrServerLifecycle` (a `SmartLifecycle`). It starts once its context has finished refreshing and stops before the context closes. The webapp `Listener` defers that start until `SchedulerService.onStartup()`, which both startup paths call once modules have started. Contexts refreshed after startup, for example when a module is installed, start their server straight away, and contexts that never go through the webapp (tests) start it on refresh as before.

The webapp never closes its application context, so that lifecycle stop does not run when OpenMRS shuts down. `Context.shutdown()` therefore calls `SchedulerService.onShutdown()` first, as it did before the move to JobRunr, and `JobRunrSchedulerService` stops the server there, before the modules and the session factory are shut down.

## Verification

- `jetty:run` with 31 modules: the server's first heartbeat comes after the module refresh, and an overdue recurring job runs once and succeeds. Without this change the same startup logs the failures above.
- `jetty:run` with 31 modules, redeploying the webapp to run `contextDestroyed()`: the server stops before the modules and the session factory are shut down. Without the shutdown change it keeps running, and its next heartbeat fails with `No suitable driver found` once the webapp has deregistered the JDBC drivers.
- `mvn test -pl api,web`: api 5523 tests, web 199 tests, 0 failures. `SchedulerServiceIT` passes 22/22.
- New `JobRunrServerLifecycleTest` covers the deferral, `JobRunrSchedulerServiceTest` covers `onStartup()` starting a deferred server and `onShutdown()` stopping it, and `ContextTest` covers the scheduler shutting down before the database.

title: TRUNK-6818: Context.closeSession() closes sessions it did not open
body:
<!--- Add a pull request title above in this format -->
<!--- real example: 'TRUNK-5111: Replace use of deprecated isVoided' -->
<!--- 'TRUNK-JiraIssueNumber: JiraIssueTitle' -->
## Description of what I changed
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
<!--- It can simply be your commit message, which you must have -->

`Context.closeSession()` (and the paired `Context.openSession()`) use a thread-local counter to count the number of open sessions. This can misfire, both if `Context.openSession()` was never called, `Context.closeSession()` can mistakenly close an unowned session. Also, if there is a `Context.openSession()` without a paired `Context.closeSession()` call (as happened in `OutboxTaskSchedulerInitializer`, the attempt to use a counter can fail by leaving the thread counting connections it did not open.

Here `Context.openSession()` wraps each session it creates in a `ContextSessionHolder` and `Context.closeSession()` closes this once all paired `openSession()` calls have been closed, but only if the session is a `ContextSessionHolder`, closing this accidental gap. Also updates `OutboxTaskSchedulerInitializer` to properly pair it's `openSession()` calls to a `closeSession` call.

Release notes

Sourced from org.owasp.encoder:encoder's releases.

OWASP Java Encoder 1.5.0

Version 1.5.0 is available from Maven Central. All nine binary/source/Javadoc JARs, four POMs, and their thirteen signatures were downloaded from Central and verified against the retained signed release files. There is no encoder-esapi:1.5.0 release.

Security and correctness

  • Fixes encoded fragments completing outer HTML or XML parser delimiters across trusted-text boundaries in JavaScript HTML/block, CDATA, and XML-comment contexts. Versions through 1.4.1 are affected. See GHSA-g8p6-7r8f-qrpv.

Compatibility and migration

Public Java APIs remain binary and source compatible with 1.4.1 for the three supported libraries. Java 8 remains the minimum runtime; packaged consumers passed on Java 8, 11, 17, 21, and 25.

The security fixes deliberately change some encoded output:

  • JavaScript HTML/block modes emit additional hexadecimal escapes while preserving the string value. Review byte snapshots, cache keys, signatures, and output-size budgets.
  • CDATA preserves parsed text but can expand to 13 output characters per input character and can change parser event boundaries.
  • XML-comment hyphens become ~ under the documented lossy policy.

The optional ESAPI adapter is retired. Version 1.4.1 is its final published release and is unsupported; migrate to direct Java Encoder APIs. Mixing the 1.4.1 adapter with the 1.5 core is not a supported migration.

title: Restore lazy loading for associations converted from hbm mappings
body:
Fixes #6642.

This adds `fetch = FetchType.LAZY` to annotated to-one associations whose hbm mapping used to be lazy. hbm `many-to-one` mappings were lazy proxies by default, but JPA's `@ManyToOne` and `@OneToOne` are eager by default. The change covers 90 associations in 30 entity classes. I checked each one against the 2.8.x hbm files and kept the ones that were `lazy="false"` (`User.person`, `User.roles`, `PatientProgram.location`) eager.

The associations behind this join are:
- ConceptName's `concept`, `creator`, `changedBy` and `voidedBy`, which were lazy in 2.8.x.
- `Condition.previousVersion` and `Condition.patient`.
- Diagnosis's `condition`, `encounter` and `patient`.
- CodedOrFreeText's `coded` and `specificName`.

Condition, Diagnosis and CodedOrFreeText have been annotation-mapped, and therefore eager, since 2.3. Their 2.2.x hbm mappings were lazy. Module code that touched these associations outside a session since 2.3 could notice the change.

Some entities were already eager on 2.3–2.8 and are outside this join graph, so I didn't change them: Encounter, Visit, Allergy, Allergen, DrugIngredient and FieldAnswer.

**Tests:** `EncounterDiagnosesFetchTest` loads an encounter whose diagnosis has a condition with a previous version, and records every statement. It asserts that no statement joins more than 30 tables. On master it fails with `statement joins 107 tables (max 30)`. With this change, the largest statement joins 15 tables. The full default api suite passes (5448 tests, 0 failures), with no LazyInitializationException.

**Runtime:** I ran this together with the other two fixes from this batch (#6640, #6641, #6642) on MySQL 8 (`mvn jetty:run`), with all 31 O3 reference application modules upgraded to Platform 3 and the full O3 reference content loaded. The O3 frontend then worked end to end for: patient registration, starting and ending a visit, vitals, conditions, allergies, lab and drug orders, lab result entry, dispensing, queueing, appointments, a form-engine form, ward admission, billing and stock items. The O3 Visits page, which failed on master with `Too many tables; MySQL can only use 61 tables in a join`, now lists every visit with its diagnoses.

title: Return HTTP 500 for uncaught exceptions
body:

title: TRUNK-6827: Forward onPersist and onRemove through ChainingInterceptor
body:
Fixes [TRUNK-6827](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/TRUNK-6827).

`ChainingInterceptor` now overrides `onPersist` and `onRemove` and forwards them to each chained interceptor. Hibernate's defaults for those delegate to `onSave` / `onDelete`, so interceptors that implement only the deprecated pair are still invoked exactly once. That covers core's `AuditableInterceptor`, `DropMillisecondsHibernateInterceptor`, `GlobalPropertyCacheInterceptor` and `RolePrivilegeCacheInterceptor`, as well as module interceptors like openmrs-module-event's.

The chain's own `onSave` / `onDelete` now delegate to `onPersist` / `onRemove`, so either entry point reaches every interceptor once. It also forwards `onInsert`, `onUpdate`, `onUpsert`, the 4-argument `onDelete`, and `preMerge` / `postMerge`, which Hibernate 7 calls and the chain was dropping. `EventInterceptor.onRemove` gets its missing `@Override`.

In a create event, the entity id is still null, because Hibernate calls `onPersist` before the id is assigned. That was already the case with `onSave`.

**Outbox:** with create events published, the transactional outbox could loop on its own rows, as it already does on 2.9.x. Saving an `OutboxEvent` publishes a `SaveDbEvent` about it, so an `@OutboxEventListener` that accepts that event (one taking `SaveDbEvent<?>` or `EntityEvent<?>`, say) made `OutboxEventInterceptor` save another `OutboxEvent`, and so on, until the heap ran out on the first create or update. Two changes stop it:
- `OutboxEventInterceptor` ignores entity events whose entity is an `OutboxEvent`.
- `OutboxEvent` is no longer `@Audited`, as on 2.9.x. With Envers on, each outbox row's audit row is published as a `SaveDbEvent<HashMap>`, which the check above can't recognise, so it went into the outbox as another row with an audit row of its own. `EnversAuditTableInitializerDatabaseIT` now treats an entity as audited only when its own class is `@Audited`, because Envers doesn't audit `OutboxEvent` through `BaseOpenmrsObject`'s annotation.

**Tests:**
- `EventInterceptorTest` covers create, update and delete through the real session factory. On master, create and delete fail (`expected: <1> but was: <0>`), while the update control passes.
- `ChainingInterceptorTest` checks that legacy-only and new-only interceptors are each called exactly once from both entry points, that "state modified" results are combined, and that the stateless and merge callbacks are forwarded.
- With only `ChainingInterceptor` reverted, 8 of these 9 tests fail.
- `OutboxEventInterceptorTest` checks that events about an `OutboxEvent` stay out of the outbox while others go in. The first test fails without the check.
- The full default api suite passes: 5458 tests, 0 failures.

**Runtime:** I ran this change on MySQL 8 (`mvn jetty:run`) with all 31 O3 reference application modules upgraded to Platform 3. All of them start, and logging in works. Creating and updating a location over REST works, with `creator`, `date_created` and `changed_by` populated, so the deprecated-API interceptors still run through the chain.

I also ran it on MySQL 8 with only the REST module, `hibernate.integration.envers.enabled=true` and a temporary `@OutboxEventListener` taking `SaveDbEvent<?>`. Creating a location over REST returns 201 and adds five outbox rows. With `@Audited` put back on `OutboxEvent`, logins fail and so does the outbox poller, with `Data too long for column 'payload'`, because each outbox row nests the previous one until the payload outgrows the MEDIUMTEXT column.

title: Resolve module enum classes in StringEnumType
body:
Fixes #6632.

`StringEnumType` now loads its enum through `OpenmrsClassLoader.getInstance()` rather than `Class.forName`, so module enums mapped with it resolve. This is the idiom `PersonAttribute`, `ModuleUtil` and `SchedulerFormValidator` already use. Core enums still resolve, because `OpenmrsClassLoader` delegates to core's loader.

The new `StringEnumTypeTest` covers three cases:
- A module enum: it compiles an enum into a temp dir that only a child loader can see, registers an `OpenmrsClassLoader` over that loader, and asserts the enum resolves. This test fails with the reported "Enum class not found" without the fix.
- A core enum (`Obs.Status`) still resolves.
- An unknown class still throws `HibernateException`.

The test puts back the shared `OpenmrsClassLoader` instance by reflection afterwards, so the swapped loader doesn't leak into later tests.

On a real server (core master, `mvn jetty:run`, MySQL 8), I ran the 22 O3 modules upgraded to 3.0 together with this change and #6631. All of them, including reporting and billing, which map their enums with `StringEnumType`, start, and UI login works.

title: Ensure core service advisors apply when modules declare FactoryBean services
body:
Fixes #6630.

Adds `ProxyFactoryBeanObjectTypePostProcessor`, a `BeanFactoryPostProcessor` registered as a static `@Bean` in `AOPConfig`. Before any bean is created, it visits every `AbstractSingletonProxyFactoryBean` definition (that is, `TransactionProxyFactoryBean`):
- It resolves the target's class from the `target` bean reference or inner bean.
- It computes the proxy class that the factory will produce.
- It records that class as `FactoryBean.OBJECT_TYPE_ATTRIBUTE`, Spring's documented way to declare a factory bean's type up front.

By-type lookups made while the auto-proxy advisors are being built can then match these definitions without instantiating them. As a result, module targets and the core services they reference are no longer created, and proxied without advisors, ahead of those advisors.

Definitions that set `proxyInterfaces`, whose target is itself a `FactoryBean`, or that can't be resolved are left alone, so they keep today's behaviour.

**Tests:**
- `ModuleFactoryBeanServiceAdvisorsTest` adds two fixture beans to the test context:
  - A metadatamapping-style `ref` target with `conceptService`/`adminService` properties.
  - A queue-style inner-bean target with an `@Autowired OrderService`.
- Without the fix, those core services lack the authorization, required-data and transaction advice, and a logged-out `conceptService.getConcept(3)` does not throw. With the fix, all 4 tests pass.
- The full default api suite passes: 5451 tests, 0 failures.

**Runtime:**
- On master, OpenMRS with 17 Platform-3-upgraded O3 modules fails to start with the error in #6630.
- With this branch running the same 17 modules (`mvn jetty:run`, MySQL 8):
  - All modules start.
  - UI login works.
  - Anonymous REST calls to core services are again refused with 401.

body:
Bumps [org.owasp.encoder:encoder](https://github.com/owasp/owasp-java-encoder) from 1.4.0 to 1.4.1.
Release notes

Sourced from org.owasp.encoder:encoder's releases.

v1.4.1 — Security release

OWASP Java Encoder 1.4.1

Version 1.4.1 is available from Maven Central. Published on 2026-09-27 UTC (2026-09-26 in America/Los_Angeles) from the original retained signed bundle. All 12 binary/source/Javadoc JARs, five POMs, and their 17 signatures were downloaded from Central and matched the original release byte for byte. Versions through 1.4.0 remain affected.

Central artifacts: encoder, encoder-jsp, encoder-jakarta-jsp, encoder-esapi, encoder-parent.

Security fixes

Upgrade all OWASP Java Encoder dependencies to 1.4.1. Versions through 1.4.0 are affected by the following issues:

  • GHSA-57jg-769q-93vh: EncodedWriter could lose encoding context when pending lookahead overflowed its output buffer, allowing CDATA or XML comment delimiters to escape and dropping or duplicating characters. The fix preserves unconsumed input across buffer flushes.
  • GHSA-q6jj-5396-8mq2: EncodedWriter could loop indefinitely when a write did not supply enough input to resolve pending lookahead. The fix retains pending input for the next write or close instead of spinning.
  • GHSA-p9ff-j89j-9xhx: long runs of U+2028 or U+2029 could cause the String overloads of Encode.forCssString and Encode.forCssUrl to throw AssertionError. The fix corrects the maximum encoded output size. The JSP/Jakarta CSS EL functions and the ESAPI CSS adapter also benefit from this fix.

The first two issues require direct use of EncodedWriter; the Encode facade, JSP/Jakarta tags, and ESAPI adapter do not call it internally. The CSS size issue affects String-returning APIs; Writer overloads and CSS tags are unaffected.

Compatibility and other changes

  • Java 8 remains the minimum runtime. Build and test with JDK 17.
  • Public method signatures, Maven coordinates, explicit JPMS module names, and historical Automatic-Module-Name values are retained.
  • The JSP, Jakarta, and ESAPI module descriptors now expose their public API dependencies transitively (#98).
  • The ESAPI adapter now uses a fixed ESAPI 2.7.0.0 dependency; tested compatibility is documented in esapi/README.md (#99).
  • Build tooling, packaged OSGi compatibility tests, project metadata, and Jakarta test dependency alignment have been updated (#90, #106).

title: TRUNK-6707: Implement full caching for Global Properties
body:
<!--- Add a pull request title above in this format -->
<!--- real example: 'TRUNK-5111: Replace use of deprecated isVoided' -->
<!--- 'TRUNK-JiraIssueNumber: JiraIssueTitle' -->
## Description of what I changed
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
<!--- It can simply be your commit message, which you must have -->

Global properties are read constantly through OpenMRS and rarely change over the course of an application execution. This PR adds aggressive, layered caching for Global Properties to reduce the number of database calls and, ultimately, speed up getting global properties. Global properties are now backed by our in-memory distributed cache. Writes to global properties will evict the value. The cache holds entries for no more than 15 minutes in case any maintenance is performed by raw SQL. As a result, implementers should expect that GP updates done outside of OpenMRS may take up to 1 hour to become effective. In most cases, GP updates will be effective immediately, but if a thread reads the cache while the write / evict is in progress, it may get a stale value. This should generally be a window of milliseconds.

This also solves TRUNK-6771 because ConfigUtil no longer maintains its own cache.

title: Clear leaked outbox rows before OutboxEventServiceTest tests
body:
\`OutboxEventServiceTest.getProcessingAndPendingEvents_shouldReturnOnlyPendingAndProcessingEvents\` fails on Linux CI depending on test order (e.g. #6594 and several other recent PR builds).

\`TestTransactionalEventAggregator\` turns every committed global property save into a \`TestAggregatedEntityEvent\` outbox row. After the module tests run, the table holds over 100 pending rows, and \`getProcessingAndPendingEvents()\` (\`order by id asc\`, limit 100) no longer returns the test's own events.

The test now deletes existing outbox rows in \`setUp()\`. The delete runs inside the test transaction, so it is rolled back after each test.

Reproduced locally by running \`ModuleInteroperabilityTest\`, \`ModuleFactoryTest\` and \`ModuleActivatorTest\` before \`OutboxEventServiceTest\` (\`-Dsurefire.runOrder=reversealphabetical\`): the test fails before the change and passes after it.

spotbugs-maven-plugin-4.10.4.1

Users who previously configured outputEncoding directly on the SpotBugs Maven Plugin must configure project.reporting.outputEncoding instead and remove it to avoid errors. Avoid redundant session attribute writes in `OpenmrsFilter` by only updating `username` and `locale` when their values have changed.

title: TRUNK-6793: Add optional OpenTelemetry metrics export
body: ## Description of what I changed OpenMRS now speaks OpenTelemetry! openmrs-core can now export OpenTelemetry metrics. bundles the OTel Java agent and attaches it when `OMRS_OTEL_ENABLED`=true. off by default. nothing changes for anyone who doesn't opt in. ### Why do we need this? Implementers currently have no standard way to see whether an openmrs server is healthy. everyone builds their own thing, in whatever shape, so nothing's shareable. OTel is a CNCF standard that basically every observability backend speaks. So instead of us picking a monitoring vendor for people, we emit a standard format and they point it wherever: _"openmrs exports standard OTel. Grab it however you like."_ **Why core and not the distro:** bahmni, kenyaEMR, ugandaEMR and the rest all build on core. distro-only means each of them reimplements it. also the attach logic has to live in startup.sh anyway, and that's here. **Why the java agent and not a JMX scraper**: runs in-process, exposes nothing. a scraper needs every deployment to open a JMX/RMI port, which is a rough default for a clinical system. ### What changed Dockerfile: downloads the agent to /openmrs/otel in the production stage, checksum-verified, same pattern as the tini and tomcat downloads. Pure java so no TARGETARCH handling needed. startup.sh: appends -javaagent: to CATALINA_OPTS when the flag is set. mirrors the existing OMRS_DEV_DEBUG_PORT block right above it. uses ${VAR-} since the script runs under -u. that's it. everything past the on/off flag is standard `OTEL_*` variables, so the config surface is the OTel spec rather than something we invented. Sample config: ``` OMRS_OTEL_ENABLED: true OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: http://alloy:4317 OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL: grpc OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: openmrs-backend OTEL_JMX_TARGET_SYSTEM: tomcat OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER: otlp OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER: none OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER: none ``` ### The cost The jar adds ~24MB to every openmrs-core image whether you use it or not. that's the real tradeoff. No runtime cost when disabled, the -javaagent flag just never gets added. ### Tested Validated end to end on the reference application: agent → gRPC → Alloy → Prometheus → Grafana. Distro PR: https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-distro-referenceapplication/pull/1069 ## Issue I worked on see https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/TRUNK-6793 ## Checklist: I completed these to help reviewers :) - [x] My IDE is configured to follow the [**code style**](https://wiki.openmrs.org/display/docs/Java+Conventions) of this project. Release notes

Sourced from org.dbunit:dbunit's releases.

3.5.1

Fixed Bugs

  • Fix a 3.5.0 regression (introduced by issue dbunit/dbunit-extension#496 fix) where FlatXmlProducer added every table from an explicitly-supplied metadata IDataSet as an empty table, not just tables actually present in the flat XML body: FlatXmlDataSetBuilder#setMetaDataSet(IDataSet) is documented as supplying column metadata only, but a broad metadata source such as a live database's full IDataSet (e.g. via DatabaseConnection#createDataSet()) was being read as if it enumerated the fixture's own tables, so DELETE_ALL/CLEAN_INSERT ended up touching every table in that broader source instead of only the ones the XML body mentions. FlatXmlProducer's issue dbunit/dbunit-extension#496 empty-table backfill now only runs when the metadata source is DTD-derived (a FlatDtdDataSet, whether parsed inline from the flat XML's own DOCTYPE or supplied via FlatXmlDataSetBuilder#setMetaDataSetFromDtd), restoring pre-3.5.0 behavior for any other explicitly-supplied metadata dataset. title: TRUNK-6784: LoggingAdvice should have a fast exit path
body:
<!--- Add a pull request title above in this format -->
<!--- real example: 'TRUNK-5111: Replace use of deprecated isVoided' -->
<!--- 'TRUNK-JiraIssueNumber: JiraIssueTitle' -->
## Description of what I changed
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
<!--- It can simply be your commit message, which you must have -->

`LoggingAdvice` is wrapped-around every service method call and provides useful logging information when the loggers are setup to display it. Most of the time, this logging is disabled; however, because `LoggingAdvice` lacks a fast exit pathway when it won't log any messages, it winds up adding some unnecessary method overhead. While the overhead here is quite small on a per-call basis, because it's invoked on every service method, the overhead can become a significant portion of a single threads CPU usage when the underlying wrapped calls are fast.

This adds some reasonable fast exit points to the `LoggingAdvice` which should trigger in the normal case where `DEBUG` and `TRACE` level logging are not enabled. Also adds some tests for `LoggingAdvice` itself. These tests pass both with and without these changes.

  • removeUnusedImports no longer fails on Java import module declarations. (#2890)

  • Default google-java-format remains 1.28.0 on JVM 17; bumps to 1.30.0 on JVM 21+; require at least 1.30.0 on JVM 25+ for import module support.
  • Bump default eclipse version to latest 4.39 -> 4.40. (#1996)
  • Document Maven skip properties spotless.skip, spotless.check.skip, and spotless.apply.skip. Goal-specific skips now live on their own mojos so they no longer leak across goals. (#3009)

title: TRUNK-6777: Cache the tokenization of LayoutTemplates
body:
<!--- Add a pull request title above in this format -->
<!--- real example: 'TRUNK-5111: Replace use of deprecated isVoided' -->
<!--- 'TRUNK-JiraIssueNumber: JiraIssueTitle' -->
## Description of what I changed
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
<!--- It can simply be your commit message, which you must have -->

We use LayoutTemplates to store how to format peoples names and addresses since our data model allows for a flexible set of fields with instance- determined meaning. These templates are called frequently, e.g., whenever we render a "full" or "short" name. In a single-threaded run, the run is dominated by the call to `getLines()` which on each invocation reparses the template. By cacheing this tokenization, we greatly speed up (~20x) the amount of time it takes to format a name. Since these templates are _very_ stable, this should be a net win on every operation that formats a user's name.

title: TRUNK-6779: Fix flaky OpenmrsConfigurationFactoryTest when running as root
body:
## Summary
- CI (Docker) runs Maven as root, which bypasses Unix file-permission bits, so `getConfigurationFiles_shouldIgnoreUnreadableFiles` was failing consistently on CI even though it passed locally.
- The test's assumption only checked that `File.setReadable(false)` returned `true`, not that the file was actually unreadable afterward — root processes can still read a file after its read bit is cleared.
- The assumption now checks `canRead()` directly, so the test skips (rather than fails) in environments where permission bits don't restrict access, such as a root-run container.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced the CI failure locally by running `mvn test` inside the `openmrs/openmrs-core:2.9.x-dev` Docker image (which runs as root) against this source.
- [x] Confirmed the fix: full `mvn test` in that same Docker image now results in `BUILD SUCCESS`.
- [x] Confirmed no regression: `OpenmrsConfigurationFactoryTest` still runs all 15 tests with 0 failures when run locally as a non-root user.

title: TRUNK-6686: Restore relevance weighting in patient search lost in the Hibernate Search 6 migration
body:
## Description

Restores query-time relevance boosting for patient/person searches to match the ranking behavior from `OpenMRS 2.6.x`. This ensures more relevant name matches are ranked appropriately after the Hibernate Search 6 migration.

### Changes

- Added query-time boosts for `personName` fields:
    - `givenName` / `familyName`: exact 8x, prefix 4x, anywhere 2x
    - `middleName` / `familyName2`: exact 4x, prefix 2x, anywhere 1x
- Added equivalent boosts for `personAttribute` searches.
- Added a regression test verifying that a `givenName` match is ranked above a `middleName` match.
- Updated existing tests to avoid relying on ordering between equally ranked results.
- Preserved and strengthened exact-match-first regression coverage.

JobRunr and JobRunr Pro 8.8.0

JobRunr 8.8.0 comes with reduced logging in case of StorageProvider exceptions, along with several enhancements and bugfixes. Quarkus users would be happy to learn that SmallRye is no longer a required dependency. JobRunr Pro 8.8.0 also introduces performance improvements for MySQL with large amounts of jobs.

  • Kotlin 2.4 support

  • Dashboard and SQL Database performance improvements (Pro)

title: TRUNK-6733: Use java-uuid-generator for entity UUIDs instead of UUID.randomUUID()
body:
## Description of what I changed

`BaseOpenmrsObject` generates its uuid in a field initialiser:

```java
private String uuid = UUID.randomUUID().toString();
```

Field initialisers run on every construction, which includes every Hibernate hydration of every
entity, where the generated value is then immediately overwritten by the uuid column read from the
database. `UUID.randomUUID()` draws from a single, JVM wide `SecureRandom` whose `engineNextBytes`
is synchronized, so every entity instantiation contends on one JVM wide monitor and the cost scales
with the number of rows a request loads.

A cryptographically strong source is not required here: uuids identify objects rather than protect
them. Access to a record is granted by privilege checks rather than by a uuid being unguessable,
and security sensitive tokens are generated separately (user activation keys use
`RandomStringUtils.randomAlphanumeric(20)`).

### What this does

All uuid generation in `api/src/main` now goes through a single helper, `org.openmrs.util.UuidUtil`,
which hands java-uuid-generator a `Random` backed by `ThreadLocalRandom`. Every thread therefore
draws from its own stream and none of them queue up behind a shared generator.

Routing everything through one helper also means the scheme can be changed in one place later.

### Three things worth flagging for reviewers

**`Generators.randomBasedGenerator()` on its own does not fix this.** With no argument, JUG falls
back to a shared `SecureRandom` singleton of its own, so the queue simply moves from one JVM wide
monitor to another. Measured at 32 threads it is 499.9 ns/uuid against a 539.8 ns/uuid baseline,
i.e. effectively no improvement. The random number generator that is passed in is what matters.

**The generator cannot be a captured `ThreadLocalRandom.current()`.** `Generators.randomBasedGenerator(Random)`
stores whatever it is handed in a field, and every thread then draws through that one reference,
whereas `current()` is documented as "Methods of this object should be called only by the current
thread, not by other threads." `UuidUtil.ThreadLocalRandomSource` is therefore a small `Random` that
calls `current()` on each draw. The JDK does the same thing internally:
`ThreadLocalRandom.ThreadLocalRandomProxy` is a private `Random` subclass whose `nextInt`,
`nextLong` and `nextDouble` delegate to `ThreadLocalRandom.current()`.

**Version 7 was measured and not used.** `TimeBasedEpochGenerator.construct()` holds a
`synchronized` block on a shared entropy buffer for every call, which reintroduces exactly the
shared monitor contention this ticket is about (111.9 ns/uuid at 32 threads). Version 4 also keeps
uuids from revealing when a record was created, which matters when they appear in URLs. `UuidUtil`
documents the single place to change should v7 be wanted later.

### Compatibility

Generated values are unchanged in form: canonical, 36 character, version 4 uuid strings that fit
the existing 38 character `uuid` column. Existing rows and their uuids are unaffected and there are
no liquibase changes in this PR, so no migration is required.

Measured over 96 million uuids generated on 32 threads, with a JFR recording using
`settings=profile` (10 ms monitor threshold, the same floor the ticket quotes):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jdk.JavaMonitorEnter` events | 49, all on `sun.security.provider.HashDrbg` | 0 |
| wall clock | 56.7 s | 0.6 s |
| uuid generation on the entity path | 539.8 ns/uuid | 5.9 ns/uuid |

A complete `new Location()` now costs 21.9 ns at 32 threads, less than 5% of what the uuid alone
used to cost.

body:

## Description of what I changed

<!--- It can simply be your commit message, which you must have -->

We added a performance test to 2.9.x to assert that its startup performance continued to be an improvement over 2.8.x. While that's true, the actual startup time difference for the platform alone is pretty minimal (~3s on my machine, slightly less on CI), meaning that it's easily swallowed by noise.

The previous version of this test relied on wall-clock time that is intuitively appealing—it is the metric we want to improve. Unfortunately, this measurement of wall-clock time also included Docker operations which do not run at deterministic speeds. This is an attempt to revise the test to work more deterministically. Specifically:

1. We now scan the logs for evidence of two optimizations applied in 2.9.x having run (both involve skipping Liquibase workloads).
2. We leverage Tomcat's logged startup time as the "wall-clock time". Because this skips the Docker overhead, this should more reliably be faster on 2.9.x than 2.8.x
